app.title: TransPrimer — Tm-guided exon–exon junction primer design for isoform-specific RT-PCR/qPCR
app.summary: The person names a gene and species, a RefSeq transcript accession, or pastes their own transcripts exon by exon. They can pick one variant from an exon-structure alignment of the gene's transcripts. The tool fetches every sibling isoform and checks whether the target has a stretch of sequence that no sibling carries. It then classifies the target as needing an ordinary primer pair, a primer that spans an exon–exon junction, or neither. The person tunes and checks primers in a designer: they drag-select a window across the junction and watch its melting temperature and the melting temperature of each arm update. They can also set the Tm range, product size and reaction conditions, and leave chosen transcripts out of the comparison. They come away with a copied primer pair that is checked to amplify only the target, or one pair that amplifies every variant for a total-expression assay.

task.text: Decide whether one transcript isoform can be amplified apart from its siblings, and design primers that do it.

data.text: Curated transcript sequences of one gene, each with its exon structure on the reference genome, compared against each other by sequence.
data.item: a transcript isoform of a gene, with its exons and mRNA sequence

stage.text: planning an isoform-specific RT-PCR/qPCR assay, before ordering primers

mechanism.text: A search box loads a gene, and a picker lays out its transcripts on one genomic axis. Analysing a target fills a verdict banner, an exon-track graph of every isoform that marks the unique regions and junctions, and a per-isoform verdict table. Clicking an accession in the graph re-targets the design. The junction workbench shows the junction sequence, where a dragged selection is evaluated live against Tm rules set in a side rail, and the chosen pair is copied out.

field.text: isoform-specific primer design for RT-PCR/qPCR in molecular biology

workflow.name: check whether a target can be told apart from its siblings, then design a probe that does it

steps.here: Search by species and gene symbol or by RefSeq accession, with typeahead. Or paste custom transcripts with exon boundaries marked by '|', or by numbers that are split for you.

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: The gene's transcripts are drawn on one genomic axis, with identical accessions folded into one row. Clicking one picks it as the target.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: A 20-nt sliding window finds sequence absent from every sibling. Each transcript is classified as EEJ-independent, EEJ-dependent or infeasible, and the graph and verdict table show the unique regions and junctions.
Transcript chips take siblings out of the comparison, and every tier and design is recomputed against the transcripts that remain.

In the junction workbench the person drag-selects a window over the splice junction. The whole oligo's Tm and each arm's Tm update live against the Tm range, ΔTm and salt/Mg²⁺/dNTP conditions set in the rail.
A partner primer is chosen within a product-size range and QC-checked for hairpin and dimer. The forward and reverse pair is copied to the clipboard.

distinctive: a junction primer must melt inside the chosen Tm range while each arm alone stays at least 15 °C below it, so it primes only across that exact splice
Tm is computed by nearest-neighbour thermodynamics with editable salt, Mg²⁺, dNTP and primer concentrations, and short arms fall back to the Wallace rule
accessions with identical sequence and exon structure are folded into one transcript, so a transcript is not compared against its own twin
every amplicon must span at least two exons, so it cannot be confused with product amplified from genomic DNA
a separate tab designs one pair that amplifies as many variants as possible at one product size, for total-expression assays
